newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador's private bank profits rise 91.4 pct in H1.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador's private bank profits rise 91.4 pct in H1.

text.p: Ecuador's private banks showed a 91.4 percent year-over-year increase in net profits in the first half of 1997, the Superintendency of Banks said late Wednesday.
Net profits in the first half rose to $64.3 million from $33.6 million in the first six months of 1996, the banking regulator said.

The improvement paralleled Ecuador's economic performance. The economy this year has emerged from a slowdown that followed a border conflict with Peru in 1995 and last year's energy crisis, a banker who asked not to be named told Reuters.
The economic trend should increase gross financing margins this year, he said.
The central bank's reference lending rates have fallen to 27 percent in June from 49 percent a year earlier.
Banco del Progreso reported the highest net profits in the first half, with $17.1 million, followed by Banco del Pichnicha, with $10.4 million, and Banco La Previsor, with $5.6 million.
Only four of the 43 private banks in the country reported losses in the first half.
The combined assets of the private banking sector at the end of the first half rose 4.9 percent to $8.4 billion from the year-earlier period.
